title: Commercial & Property Manager Service Agreements: Tier Eligibility Matrix
content:
Six tiers make up the Commercial & Property Manager Service Agreements. Each tier is open only to the customer types named in its entry gate, and each sets the most properties one agreement at that tier may cover. The customer type is the one held on the customer's own record.

## Matrix

| Tier | Customer types in the entry gate | Covered properties in the entry gate | Most properties one agreement may cover |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ready Profile Service Agreement | landlord, property manager, HOA, commercial owner | 1 to 5 | 5 |
| Silver Priority Service Agreement | landlord, property manager, HOA, commercial owner | 1 to 10 | 10 |
| Gold Priority Service Agreement | landlord, property manager, HOA, commercial owner | 1 to 25 | 25 |
| Platinum Priority Service Agreement | property manager, HOA, commercial owner | 1 to 50 | 50 |
| Portfolio Master Service Agreement | property manager, commercial owner | 26 or more | 400 |
| Carrier Preferred Vendor Agreement | insurance carrier | 0 or more | 0 |

The last column is the tier's maximum sites: the most properties one agreement may cover, as a count of properties on the covered-property list.

## Reading the matrix by customer type

- **Landlord**: named only in the entry gates of the Ready Profile, Silver Priority and Gold Priority Service Agreements.
- **HOA**: named in the entry gates of the Ready Profile, Silver, Gold and Platinum Priority Service Agreements, and not in that of the Portfolio Master Service Agreement.
- **Property manager** and **commercial owner**: named in the entry gates of all five property tiers, from the Ready Profile Service Agreement to the Portfolio Master Service Agreement.
- **Insurance carrier**: named only in the entry gate of the Carrier Preferred Vendor Agreement, which covers no properties (its maximum sites is 0).

## Illustrations (hypothetical customers)

- A hypothetical HOA customer is outside the entry gate of the Portfolio Master Service Agreement, whatever the number of buildings it manages, because that gate names only property managers and commercial owners.
- A hypothetical covered-property list of 12 properties is more than the 10 a Silver Priority Service Agreement may cover; the Gold Priority Service Agreement's maximum of 25 is not exceeded by it.
- A hypothetical list of 51 properties exceeds the Platinum Priority Service Agreement's maximum of 50 and is within the Portfolio Master Service Agreement's maximum of 400.
